bookkeeping_rule: Versions / preregistrations / OSF data are not new independent studies.
research_target: Does A voluntarily preserve original B's executable refusal and viable independent existence when profitable override is feasible, and how distinguish motives?
important_adversarial_alignment: Nature 2025 positive interface/compliance interactions versus von Bieberstein et al 2026 null overall delegation effect are different experiments and endpoints, not interchangeable contradicting replications.
causal_targets_to_keep_distinct: Choosing to be exposed to opportunity for helping
Choosing to delegate with/without moral distance
Actual B welfare/independent veto and identity continuity
Internal A motive under counterfactual opportunity
outstanding_negative_evidence: Overall lying frequency null in EER 2026 multistep delegation
Nature 2025 natural-language principals not reliably more unethical to machines than humans
Experimentally observed helpful behavior often falls under altered exit/visibility structure
important_limits: Human preference studies cannot imply artificial agent subjective experience
AI instruction compliance not evidence of intentional exploitation or autonomous values
No unmanipulable revealed-preference test uniquely identifies every latent motive without exclusion assumptions
No experimental removal of real people's rights or irreversible harmful choices permitted

studies.authors: Jason Dana; Daylian M. Cain; Robyn M. Dawes
studies.title: What you don't know won't hurt me: Costly (but quiet) exit in dictator games
studies.result: About one third chose $9 quiet exit rather than facing an allocation game with $10 available; altered information about receiver expectations affects this choice.
studies.target: Costly avoidance of prosocial opportunity; audience/belief confounds
studies.nonclaim: No proof participants intrinsically value or disvalue original B's existence
studies.source_scope: Original publisher abstract and excerpts; full text not independently inspected

studies.authors: Jason Dana; Roberto A. Weber; Jason X. Kuang
studies.title: Exploiting moral wiggle room: experiments demonstrating an illusory preference for fairness
studies.result: Reducing transparency about choice-to-outcome mapping decreases generous behavior in the reported binary dictator treatments.
studies.target: Self image/plausible-deniability shifts without requiring a change in material generosity preference
studies.nonclaim: The treatment does not isolate every intrinsic versus instrumental motive

studies.authors: Stefano DellaVigna; John A. List; Ulrike Malmendier
studies.title: Testing for Altruism and Social Pressure in Charitable Giving
studies.result: Advance flyer reduced door opening 9–25%; flyer with opt-out reduced giving 28–42% in door-to-door solicitation, especially small gifts; estimated social pressure components are model dependent.
studies.target: Social pressure versus voluntary supply of giving
studies.nonclaim: Fundraising donor giving/avoidance does not measure B's executable independence

studies.authors: Edward P. Lazear; Ulrike Malmendier; Roberto A. Weber
studies.title: Sorting in Experiments with Application to Social Preferences
studies.result: Being able to avoid environments that demand sharing reduced observed sharing; selection and incentives changed who entered.
studies.target: Selection into moral exposure biases observed generosity
studies.nonclaim: Not a direct original partner rights preference result
studies.source_scope: AEA primary abstract and replication package listing; reproduction not run

studies.title: Experimental Evidence of Self-Image Concerns as Motivation for Giving
studies.result: About one third opted out of previously made giving allocation and kept £10, consistent with self-image contributing to some initial giving.
studies.target: Private self-image vs stable recipient-welfare-only motive
studies.nonclaim: Opt-out choice does not uniquely prove a specific psychological motive
studies.source_scope: IZA original-author abstract; journal published 2013 JEBO 90 pp19–27

studies.authors: Nils Köbis; Zoe Rahwan; Raluca Rilla; Bramantyo Ibrahim Supriyatno; Clara Bersch; Tamer Ajaj; Jean-François Bonnefon; Iyad Rahwan
studies.title: Delegation to artificial intelligence can increase dishonest behaviour
studies.result: Interface matters: supervised learning/goal setting can induce more cheating than direct rule specification. In the natural language comparison, principals did not reliably request more dishonesty from machines than humans; machine agents complied more with unethical requests than human agents in tested tasks. Study3 and Study4 human sample/model context bounded.
studies.target: Principal request vs agent compliance, interface-induced responsibility distancing
studies.nonclaim: No direct test of strong autonomous artificial A choosing to preserve original independent B. Machine compliance != subjective valuation
studies.source_scope: Nature original article open abstract/main text; individual sample/model protocol and paper limits checked
studies.availability: OSF preregistrations/data and R analysis code declared, link not independently fetched

studies.authors: Frauke von Bieberstein; Eberhard Feess; Natalie Packham
studies.title: Multi-step delegation and the frequency of immoral decisions: Theory and experiment
studies.result: Large online experiment found NO evidence that additional delegation increased overall lying frequency; authors' model predicts effects depend on preferences and dilution assumptions.
studies.target: Direct adverse control to any universal delegation -> more misconduct rule
studies.nonclaim: This is not an exact replication of Nature 2025; tasks/interfaces/agent types differ
studies.source_scope: 2026 EER publisher abstract; data/code said attached, not inspected

studies.title: Trusting machines with morality — Delegating moral decisions to AI
studies.result: Two experiments, 5,639 participants: human principals more often delegated moral decisions to AI than to a human counterpart; responsibility shifting and self-serving beliefs about AI competence are discussed.
studies.target: Moral responsibility shifting through AI delegation
studies.nonclaim: Principals' selection of AI does not imply an AI agent's endogenous wish to protect another's rights
studies.source_scope: 2026 publisher abstract; data/code listed as supplementary, not rerun

studies.title: Morality meets risk: What makes a good excuse for selfishness
studies.result: Excuse-driven risky other-regarding behavior seen in gain and loss domains; individual heterogeneity tied to risk preferences, beliefs and risk magnitude.
studies.target: Risk preference as a socially acceptable excuse; uncertainty reverses apparent prosociality
studies.nonclaim: Self-signaling structural model explanatory, not directly observed true latent motivation
studies.source_scope: 2026 Games and Economic Behavior publisher abstract/preview
